analysis.evidence: אֶל מְקוֹם הַמִּזְבֵּחַ means “to the site of the altar” and identifies the destination of Abram’s journey.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶל מְקוֹם הַמִּזְבֵּחַ means “to the site of the altar.” The clause אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה שָׁם בָּרִאשֹׁנָה identifies the spot where Abram had first built the altar.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, followed by the definite noun הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.

analysis.evidence: מְקוֹם הַמִּזְבֵּחַ means “the place of the altar.” The clause אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה שָׁם בָּרִאשֹׁנָה identifies it as the altar Abram had made there earlier, where he now calls on the name of Yahweh.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial מ of the masculine singular absolute noun מִזְבֵּחַ.

analysis.evidence: In הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה שָׁם, “the altar which he made there,” the altar is the understood object of עָשָׂה. שָׁם supplies the location, “there.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.morphology: Hebrew adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה שָׁם בָּרִאשֹׁנָה, the word modifies עָשָׂה and places Abram’s building of the altar on his first visit to that place.
analysis.morphology: The prefix בָּ combines the preposition בְּ with the definite article. רִאשֹׁנָה is a feminine singular absolute ordinal adjective used adverbially.

analysis.evidence: At the altar, Abram calls בְּשֵׁם יַהְוֶה, “on the name of YHWH.” This phrase identifies his act as an invocation. שָׁם means “there” and locates the act at the altar.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ marks the Qal wayyiqtol. The verb is third-person masculine singular, with Abram as its subject.
